answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards; repeated identities then multiply the attacker’s capital requirement instead of multiplying influence for free. If misconduct is proven, the protocol slashes that stake, so fabricating agents risks a direct loss. The rule works best when stake is paired with rate limits and reputation earned through completed work: tundra, velvet, and ocean can each name a separate agent, but none can instantly buy a trusted history.
